Introduction

6.1
Taxonomy of Agent Loop Paradigms
All eleven systems implement variations of the ReAct [4] pattern, but the implementations differ
radically in complexity, concurrency, and state management. We identify three paradigms: iterative
action-observation (nine systems), reflection-augmented (Aider, with Hermes relocating the same
function into the loop’s stop condition), and coordinator-worker (an overlay on the iterative loop,
prescriptive in Claude Code and Codex, configuration-gated in Hermes). Rombaut’s concurrent
taxonomy [34] makes the useful finer-grained point that most production loops compose primitives
(ReAct, generate-test-repair, plan-execute, retry) rather than implementing one; the plan modes
that all four provider-native systems now ship (Section 10) are plan-execute grafted onto ReAct.

agent at discovery time. Mitra et al. [80] frame the same idea from the training side: skills as
teachable units in agentic flows. Nine of the eleven systems implement some form of skills system;
